The factional National Chairman of the African Democratic Congress, Nafiu Bala Gombe, has urged former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar to return to his ward and formally register as a member of the party, promising to consider appointing him chairman of its 2027 Presidential Campaign Council. Bala made the appeal in a statement sent to our correspondent on Sunday, while responding to a question on the faction’s next move after the Independent National Electoral Commission’s decision to await the outcome of the Court of Appeal proceedings before taking further action on the ADC leadership dispute. Rather than announce a fresh legal or political step in response to INEC’s position, the factional chairman disclosed that the party had held a strategic engagement with its presidential, governorship and National Assembly candidates to harmonise campaign plans ahead of the 2027 general elections. The meeting, held at the NCI International Conference Centre, Kaduna, was attended by the faction’s presidential candidate, Prof. Chris Uba; vice-presidential candidate, Dr Shamsuddeen Modibbo Barkindo; and other candidates from across the country. In the statement signed by the faction’s Director of Media and Public Affairs, Christopher Okechukwu, Bala called on Atiku to “sheathe his sword” and return to his ward to register as a bona fide member of the ADC. Bala added that he would consider appointing Atiku as chairman of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council upon his registration. Anosike plans industrial clusters, housing estates for Osisioma 2027: Tinubu orders Masari, Badaru to reconcile APC leaders Water stopped while I was shaving in Aso Rock – Tinubu The statement quoted him as saying that Atiku’s “wealth of political experience, national reach and deep understanding of governance would be a major asset to the party” in its bid to dislodge the All Progressives Congress-led Federal Government and provide Nigerians with an alternative. The factional chairman also urged its candidates to return to their constituencies, mobilise support at the grassroots and work in unity with party structures at all levels. He said the engagement reaffirmed the faction’s commitment to internal cohesion, inclusive leadership and a coordinated nationwide campaign ahead of the 2027 elections. Attempts by our correspondent to reach Atiku’s ADC National Publicity Secretary, Bolaji Abdullahi, for his reaction to the call by Nafiu Bala’s faction asking former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar to register afresh with the party to qualify for appointment as its campaign chairman were unsuccessful. Calls and text messages sent to Abdullahi had not been responded to as of the time of filing this report. Chima Azubuike
